questions.q: Where does SQL authentication store the credential a client connects with?
options: In Microsoft Entra ID exclusively
A username and a hash of the password, stored inside the SQL Server/Azure SQL engine itself
In the client application's source code only
It doesn't store a credential at all
questions.explain: SQL authentication is the model where the login's credential lives and is checked inside the database engine, which is exactly what creates the password-management and no-MFA problems.

questions.q: What does FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER mean in CREATE LOGIN [alex@ltvacademy.com] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER?
options: It creates a brand-new password stored in SQL Server
It only works for on-premises SQL Server, never Azure SQL
It disables authentication for that login entirely
The identity is not stored in SQL Server at all — it's a reference to an identity that already exists in Microsoft Entra ID
questions.explain: Entra-authenticated logins reference an external identity; authentication happens against Entra ID rather than against a credential stored in the database.

questions.q: Which capability does Entra authentication provide that SQL authentication does not?
options: Automatic data compression
Automatic table partitioning
Built-in multi-factor authentication enforced through Entra's conditional access
Faster query execution
questions.explain: MFA is enforced by Entra ID itself for Entra-authenticated logins, with no extra configuration on the SQL side — SQL authentication has no equivalent built-in mechanism.

questions.q: Why is disabling access centralized under Entra authentication but not under SQL authentication?
options: Entra authentication cannot be disabled once granted
Disabling a person in Entra ID immediately stops every Entra-authenticated login they had, while SQL logins must each be found and disabled individually per system
SQL authentication automatically disables all logins the moment one is disabled
There is no difference between the two models for disabling access
questions.explain: Each system with its own SQL logins is its own identity silo, so removing access means hunting down every login separately — Entra's centralized identity avoids that entirely.

questions.q: What does this lesson say authentication answers, versus what authorization (covered in later lessons) answers?
options: Authentication and authorization are the same concept
Authentication determines table permissions directly
Authorization happens before authentication in every case
Authentication proves who is connecting; authorization determines what that identity is allowed to do once connected
questions.explain: A successful login only proves identity — GRANT, DENY, REVOKE, and role membership (Lessons 21-23) are what determine what that identity can actually do.
